faqLeft.q: What engine does the Range Rover Sport SV use?
faqLeft.a: The Range Rover Sport SV / P635 uses the BMW S68 — a 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8. It's part of BMW's hot-vee engine family, sharing architecture with the S63 and N63 engines. It was introduced with the L461 generation in 2023.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Range Rover Sport SV engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £6,500 for the BMW S68. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my Range Rover Sport SV?
faqLeft.a: The Range Rover Sport SV uses the BMW S68. Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm your exact spec before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild BMW S68 Range Rover Sport SV engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace timing chains, valve seals, coolant components, and bearings as standard on every S68 rebuild, following the established hot-vee pattern.

faqLeft.q: Do you supply used Range Rover Sport SV engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Range Rover Sport SV if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does a Range Rover Sport SV engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most Range Rover Sport SV owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.

faqRight.q: Do you rebuild BMW S68 Range Rover Sport SV engines?
faqRight.a: Yes. We replace timing chains, valve seals, coolant components, and bearings as standard on every S68 rebuild.
